dietSummary: A smasher: cracks snails, hermit crabs, crabs and clams with its clubs, and eats small fish. Takes frozen prawn, krill and mysis 2-3 times a week.
temperamentSummary: Bold, clever and alone. Lives in a U-shaped burrow it digs in the sand, watches the tank with its swivelling eyes and hunts by day.
careNotes: Its clubs shoot out at up to 23 metres a second (over 80 km/h), one of the fastest strikes in the animal world, hard enough to crack snail shells and even aquarium glass.
It digs a U-shaped burrow in the sand with two openings and carries sand and rubble out to keep it open: give it at least 5 cm (2 in) of sand near the rock.
Not reef safe for the cleanup crew: snails, hermits, crabs and shrimp are its food, and a small fish that comes too close can be grabbed.
Its eyes have 12 kinds of colour receptors (we have 3) and see polarized light.
Keep one per tank. It can live for many years and gets to know its keeper.
